summary: Phase 3 audit of jfrog-devops at v1.2.0, applied as v1.3.0. Verified against JFrog CLI 2.117.0 executed locally, not from training data. Found and fixed: (1) the SaaS-regions claim was INVERTED, JFrog Cloud has three Israeli regions (AWS Tel Aviv, Azure Israel Central, GCP me-west1 Tel Aviv), and the claim had been carried unverified from v1.1.1 through two audits; (2) `jf scan --format=spdx` does not exist and the CLI rejects it; (3) POST /api/v1/sbom is not a real endpoint; (4) `jf audit --fail --min-severity=High` was presented as a CI gate but evaluates no policy without --watches/--project/--repo-path; (5) the US-export-controls gotcha described behavior Xray does not have; (6) `jf docker scan` cannot scan an ML repo path; (7) frogbot@v2 is in sunset, setup-jfrog-cli v5 exists, CLI is 2.117.0 not 2.103.0; (8) the Hugging Face June 2026 deadline has passed; (9) the mycompany.jfrog.io placeholder resolves to a real deactivated JFrog tenant, a credential-leak vector.
decisions_made: Bumped 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 (minor: correctness fixes across auth, SBOM, CI gating, regions, and version pins; no scope change).
RETIRED the SaaS-regions claim outright rather than editing it. It was wrong, and it had been marked 'Carried from v1.1.1' and passed through two audits unverified.

Deleted the US-export-controls gotcha as unverifiable. Xray policy types are security, license, operational risk, malicious packages, and JAS findings. There is no export-control dimension, so the described alert cannot occur.
Dropped the Sunday-Thursday deploy gotcha and the Israeli-SSO gotcha as filler: true-but-generic and unverifiable respectively, neither JFrog-specific.
Added the JFrog-is-an-Israeli-company angle as the replacement Israeli hook. Verifiable and procurement-relevant, unlike what it replaced.
Did NOT add AppTrust, jf skills, jf mcp, jf setup, jf hf, jf evd coverage or the missing setup path this cycle. All logged to optimization-log.json for the next pass.
scripts/ REST endpoints re-verified and left unchanged; only the placeholder hostname was swapped.
PROCESS CHANGE: claims marked 'carried from a prior version' are now re-verified against source rather than inherited. Two of this pass's worst findings were inherited claims.

Replaced the Pipelines EOL citation: jfrog.com/help/r/jfrog-release-information/pipelines-end-of-life returns HTTP 200 but serves a legacydocs DIRECTORY INDEX, not an EOL page. A status-code-only link check passes it. The canonical page is docs.jfrog.com/releases/docs/pipeline-deprecation-end-of-life, which confirms the May 1 2026 date verbatim. The claim was right; the citation was a soft-404.

Removed the 'JFrog Platform Documentation' reference row: jfrog.com/help/r/jfrog-platform-administration-documentation now lands on the generic 'Welcome to JFrog Docs' homepage, so its stated purpose (repository management, permissions, HA setup) no longer describes the destination.

Rewrote the curl auth examples to read $JF_URL and $JF_ACCESS_TOKEN from the environment instead of hardcoding a host and pasting a literal token. Removes the last placeholder URL from the gate's input and keeps tokens out of shell history.
out_of_scope: AppTrust and the Evidence/jf evd namespace: launched Sept 2025, missed by the v1.2.0 audit, still uncovered. Highest-value addition for the next pass, since it supersedes build-info promotion as the current promotion model.

jf skills (Artifactory as an agent-skill registry), jf mcp (JFrog MCP server for Claude Code and Cursor), jf setup, jf hugging-face, jf sbom-enrich, jf curation-audit, jf exchange-oidc-token: all absent, all logged.

The missing setup path (how to actually create repositories, the local/remote/virtual model, Xray indexing onboarding, and an end-to-end policy-to-watch-to-gate walkthrough). The four Examples describe outcomes without commands. Structural, deferred.

Self-managed pricing figures (~$27k/yr Pro X, ~$48k/yr Enterprise X) remain sourced only to third-party trackers, one of which is 403-blocked. Still confidence: medium, unverified against JFrog directly.
